title: Fictional direct state constitutional claim against Director Beta, official capacity

parent.objective: Maintain a source-pinned claim matrix for one fictional direct state constitutional claim against one official in official capacity.
parent.milestone: Claim matrix declared, adequate-state-remedy analyzed, and governing and adverse authority read

goal: State the fictional claim's elements, adequate-state-remedy analysis, threshold defense, adverse authority, remedy, limitations and justiciability.
non_goals: Predict the outcome of any claim or defense.
File, serve, or send anything to any person or court.

allowed: Declare the claim matrix and check every cited source resolves.
Record primary-source reviews of the governing and adverse authority.
prohibited: Cite a real statute, case, party, or authority.
Treat an allegation as fact before a bound primary-source review.

defendants.role: Director of the fictional Gamma Licensing Office alleged to have revoked the plaintiff's license.

assertions.assertion: Director Beta directed the fictional Gamma Licensing Office on 2026-02-01.
Under fictional Synthetic State Constitution article 1, a direct claim lies against an official in official capacity when no adequate state remedy exists.
Director Beta revoked the plaintiff's fictional license on 2026-02-01 without a hearing.
Fictional Doe v. Gamma Licensing Office holds that review under fictional Synthetic Administrative Review Code section 5 is an adequate state remedy for a license revocation.
Fictional Synthetic Administrative Review Code section 5 allows review only within ten days of a revocation.
The fictional review window had closed before the plaintiff received notice of the revocation.
Fictional Synthetic Limitations Code section 4 sets a three-year period for a direct state constitutional claim.
The claim accrued on the fictional revocation date, 2026-02-01.
Under fictional Synthetic State Constitution article 1, reinstatement is available against an official in official capacity.

claims.statement: Director Beta, in an official capacity, revoked the plaintiff's fictional license without a hearing, violating a fictional state constitutional right.
claims.legal_question: Does the fictional revocation without a hearing support a direct claim against Director Beta officially under fictional Synthetic State Constitution article 1?
claims.right: Fictional state constitutional right to a hearing before a license revocation (a stand-in that states no real constitutional holding).

elements.requirement: Action by the official in an official capacity.
Deprivation of the fictional hearing right.

threshold_defenses.defense: An adequate state remedy (fictional administrative review) bars the direct claim.
threshold_defenses.rebuttal: The fictional review window closed before notice, so the remedy was not available.

limitations.prerequisites: No fictional notice-of-claim prerequisite is declared for this claim in this worked example.

justiciability.standing: The fictional revocation is a present injury traceable to Director Beta and redressable by reinstatement.
justiciability.mootness_and_prospective_relief: The fictional license remains revoked, so reinstatement is not moot.

adequate_state_remedy.summary: Fictional administrative review exists, but its window closed before notice.

claims.next_action: Confirm from the fictional revocation order when notice was given relative to the review window.
